localised_description: The Father of Darkness is served loudly, and the people are quiet.
The temples stand unattended and the sermons go unsaid.
The forges of Zharr-Naggrund answer to one voice, and it is his.
No hand guides the forges. Output slips and no one is blamed.
Every debt in the Dark Lands is written down, and he holds the book.
The books go unbalanced and the tribute arrives light.
The outer holds are watched, and the watchers are paid on time.
The marches keep themselves, badly and at their own expense.
He carries the Sorcerer-Prophets' word down the Tower, unaltered.
The Tower's word arrives late, and altered on the way.
He counts the work gangs, and the gangs know he counts them.
Uncounted, the work gangs move at their own pace.
What comes back from a battlefield is his to sort and his to sell.
The spoils are picked over by whoever reaches them first.
The black rock comes up faster when somebody is counting the carts.
The quarries run at the pace of the laziest overseer in them.
The roads out of Zharr are his, and they are quicker than they were.
The roads are unwatched, and the caravans take the long way round.
Brick and slag leave his kilns cheaper than anyone can explain.
The kilns burn on unwatched, and the bill still arrives.
The hobgoblin tribes that work the ash fields march cheap for whoever feeds them.
The ash fields go untended, and the hobgoblins want more to march.
His clerks know which door to knock on, and when.
The clerks knock on the wrong doors and are turned away.
He knows what a warrior costs, and he pays no more than that.
Every company is hired at whatever it asks for.
Raiding is an accounting exercise, and he keeps the account.
The raiders keep their own accounts, and most of the takings.
Nothing moves in Zharr-Naggrund that the Crown did not set moving.
localised_title: An Iron Grip on the Court

localised_description: The parties argue, and then they do as they are told.
The Crown is first among the parties, and no more than first.
No decree passes without a bargain struck.
The parties rule and the Crown is consulted, when there is time.
No one rules Zharr-Naggrund. Its Sorcerer-Prophets sit in council.
The eldest voice is the strongest, and it speaks for Hashut.
The priest-artificers rule from the forges.
Rank in the court is won in the field.
Fear holds the court as the chain holds the slave.
Everything in the Dark Lands has a price.
The overseers work the stock as they always have.
More are taken and they are driven hard, and they break.
The stock is fed and kept, and fewer are taken.
Every forge has its quota, and the stock pays for it.
What cannot be held is burned, and its people with it.
The Crown takes its tithe, as it always has.
The roads are opened to more convoys, and the vassals pay less.
Every route pays the Ledger, and the cargo is worth less.
The mines come first, and the convoys carry less.
The convoy overseers are chartered, and the other houses resent it.
The rites are kept, as they always have been.
Hashut's fires are fed without stint, and building waits on them.
Seats in the Tower are sold, and the priests' favour cools.
The Lore of Hashut is taught more widely, and more carelessly.
The Daemonsmiths are licensed, and the priests resent it.
The levy is raised as it always has been.
The Hell-Forge works without leave, and the infantry pays for it.
The legions stand ready, and the guns wait.
The old grudge against the Dwarfs is fed, and the labour pays for it.
The guns come first, and every shooter costs more.
A governor of the court sits here, and the province knows it.
Your own men hold it, and they are watched.
The temples take the province in hand and it grows for Hashut.
Forge-guild overseers run the province like a workshop floor.
The slavers work the province to the bone and account for every hour.
A garrison town under a soldier costs less to keep than it should.
Brokers keep the province's books, and the tribute arrives whole.
Tower clerks read everything that passes through, and pass it on.
The caravan men keep the roads open whatever the season.
The old clans hold it, and men come back to the muster faster.
An envoy of the court is keeping order here.
An envoy of the court is driving the forges here.
An envoy of the court is driving the mines here harder.
An envoy of the court is seeing that fewer Labourers are worked to death here.
The Ancestors are honoured in every hall, and the hold is quiet.
The shrines stand unattended and the old names go unspoken.
Every forge in the hold answers to one hammer, and it is his.
No master stands at the great anvil. The work slips and no one is blamed.
Every debt the hold is owed is written down, and he holds the book.
The books go unbalanced and the tithe arrives light.
The gate is watched, and the watchers are paid on time.
The gate keeps itself, badly and at the hold's expense.
Every wrong is written in his hand. From the next Age of Reckoning, fewer grudges need settling.
The Book goes unkept. From the next Age of Reckoning, more grudges need settling.
The underways are his, and they are quicker than they were.
The underways go unwatched, and the traders take the long way round.
He counts every cart that comes up the shaft, and the miners know he counts.
Uncounted, the miners dig at their own pace.
What comes back from a battlefield is his to weigh and his to store.
The spoils are picked over by whoever reaches them first.
Stone is cut to his measure, and the halls rise for less.
The stonecutters work at the pace of the slowest of them.
He knows what a warrior costs, and he pays no more than that.
Every clan is mustered at whatever it asks for.
The hold's ale is the best in the mountains, and the trade in its fine work follows it.
The brewhouse goes unkept, and the hold's fine work sells for less.
The holdfarms are tended, and the hold grows.
The holdfarms go untended, and the hold grows slowly.
The old books are kept and read, and new work comes quicker for it.
The lore goes unread, and new work comes slowly.
Every clan banner is counted, and the Grudge Settlers march cheaper for it.
The banners go uncounted, and the Grudge Settlers ask more to march.
Nothing moves in the hold that the throne did not set moving.
localised_title: An Iron Grip on the Court

localised_description: The clans argue, and then they do as they are told.
The throne is first among the clans, and no more than first.
No decree passes without a bargain struck.
The clans rule and the throne is consulted, when there is time.
The eldest of the clans sit in council, and the throne hears them out.
The Ancestors set down how a hold is ruled, and the priests read it aloud.
The master smiths rule from the forge, and the anvil keeps the time.
The king rules from the shield wall, and so does every dwarf who would follow him.
An oath sworn in the hold is kept, or it is written down.
Every debt is counted, and the throne keeps the count.
The clans work as their fathers worked.
The miners go deeper, and the holdfarms go short of hands.
The holdfarms are tended first, and the mines wait.
Only marked work leaves the forge, and the forge eats the hours.
The halls are raised and widened, and the counting-houses pay.
The throne takes its tithe, as it always has.
The underways are opened to trade, and the vassal holds pay less.
Every hall pays the Reckoners, and the traders pay more at the gate.
The Oathgold is hoarded, and the roads are left to keep themselves.
The holds are chartered to trade their craft, and the warriors pay for it.
The rites are kept, as they always have been.
Valaya's hearths are kept warm, and the loremasters go short.
The runesmiths are given their head, and the shrines are given less.
The old books are opened, and the holdfarms lose their hands to them.
The forge is licensed to work without the priests' leave.
The clans are mustered as they always have been.
Grudge Settlers march at the throne's cost, and the counting-houses pay.
The guns come first, and every warrior costs more.
The clans march in strength, and the guns wait.
The engineers drill the guns and the thunderers, and every recruit costs more.
A governor of the throne sits here, and the province knows it.
Your own men hold it, and they are watched.
The priests keep the province, and every grudge in it is remembered.
The Forgewrights run the province like a forge floor, and the Oathgold comes in.
The Deepdelvers work the seams, and what the battlefields yield is counted.
A hold under a thane costs less to keep than it should.
The Reckoners keep the province's books, and the tithe arrives whole.
The Runesmiths read everything that passes through, and pass it on.
The Underway Wardens keep the roads open whatever the season.
The Hearth Clans hold it, and men come back to the muster faster.
An envoy of the throne is keeping order here.
An envoy of the throne is seeing that the forges here pay their Oathgold.
An envoy of the throne is seeing to the holdfarms here.
An envoy of the throne is mustering the clans here for less.
